title: Forget Suno. New BEST local AI music generator is here! (title from repo catalog .prism/shared/pot/catalog_local.json; no description file present)
core_takeaway: A new open-weights music generation model (spoken as 'UA2'/'YuE 2' in the auto-captions, exact spelling unverified without a description file) generates a full song by first writing an editable ABC-notation score for the vocal and instrumental parts, then rendering audio from that score. Because the score is an intermediate artifact, it can do things closed tools cannot: cover versions of an existing track, melody transfer, key changes major-to-minor, and lyric swaps across languages. It runs locally in ComfyUI on a quantized checkpoint that fits under 4GB of VRAM, and the presenter's benchmark chart puts it above Suno v6 and v5.5 on a song-quality index while still trailing Suno v5.
key_points: The model generates an intermediate ABC-style notation (vocal melody + instrumental melody, key, tempo) and uses that score as the backbone for the audio render, which is what makes editing and covers possible.

Reference-audio mode accepts an existing track and lets you choose melody-only or full-song reference: demos convert Auld Lang Syne into jazz funk, a Beethoven track into theatrical hard rock, and Jingle Bells into a minor key.
Multilingual vocals demonstrated: Spanish flamenco, Russian folktronica, Korean emo, plus English jazz and 1930s boogie-woogie.

Claimed benchmark (song quality index) beats MiniMax Music and 'AEP 1.5' (likely ACE-Step 1.5, caption-garbled) among open models, and beats Suno v6 and v5.5 among closed models, but scores under Suno v5.

Distribution is a ComfyUI workflow JSON plus two downloads: a 1.4GB audio encoder into models/audio_encoders and a checkpoint into models/checkpoints (BF16 is 7.8GB, quantized is 3.96GB for sub-4GB VRAM).
Generation of a full song took just over two minutes on a laptop RTX 5000-class GPU with 16GB VRAM; the demo used 32 steps and a fixed seed of 7 (same seed + same prompt reproduces the same song).
The decode node has two variants: regular decode above roughly 12GB VRAM, tiled decode below it, wired by rerouting the connection in the graph.
Licensing is split: code and docs are Apache 2.0, but the model weights carry a Creative Commons non-commercial license, so monetizing generations is legally unclear.

The presenter also drives the model from an agent (GPT Astra or GLM) to iteratively edit a song by text prompt, e.g. 'keep the melody and lyrics but make it more jazzy through reharmonization', then 'remove the guitar'.
why_it_matters: A generative model that emits an editable symbolic intermediate before rendering is exactly the architecture a tooling suite can hook into: the score is inspectable state an agent can diff, version, and mutate, instead of an opaque prompt-to-waveform black box. Because it ships as a ComfyUI graph, it slots into an existing node-based automation surface and can be driven headlessly by an agent loop. The non-commercial weights license is the constraint to design around before it goes anywhere near a product.
